source.title: Asana cleared 5 years of engineering work in 2 weeks with Codex
source.date_basis: Visible article date and article page content.

qualifying_findings.summary: Asana reports using Codex to migrate away from Enzyme in roughly two weeks, with people reviewing and approving proposed changes and with stated model/infrastructure costs around 12000 USD compared with a prior multi-year staffing estimate.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Large agent-assisted migrations should be planned as reviewable, costed change programs, not only prompt experiments. Local practice should preserve human approval, migration test evidence, and cost baselines for long-horizon modernization work.
local_practice_implications: Source-workflow pages can use this as evidence that migration tasks need explicit review and approval gates.
Verification pages can treat test-suite replacement as an acceptance-gate exercise, not a bulk rewrite alone.
Adoption pages can track model and infrastructure spend as part of the operating model for agent-led modernization.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, route broad product and company facts upstream; keep only migration workflow, review, cost, and acceptance implications locally.

source.title: Coding agent cost management: a radically new practice, and a badly misunderstood one
source.date_basis: Visible byline date on article page.

qualifying_findings.summary: PointFive frames coding-agent cost management as an emerging ownership gap, citing public examples where rapid adoption exhausted budgets or ended pilots and asking which function owns agent spend.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Team adoption guidance should assign budget ownership, usage telemetry, thresholds, and escalation paths before agents become default development infrastructure.
local_practice_implications: Adoption operating agreements should include cost-owner and budget-burn fields.
Governance infrastructure should join usage metrics with model/provider cost data.
Runtime surfaces should expose per-task or per-agent cost before teams scale parallel coding-agent work.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Verify cited third-party examples if ingest turns this into durable local guidance; do not duplicate vendor or analyst background locally.

source.title: Our AI Code Review Workflow, 7 Months Later

qualifying_findings.summary: Atomic Object describes moving from hand-written code with agent assistance toward agent-written code plus close human review, and says its AI review workflow works only because someone maintains it continuously.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: AI code review checks should be treated as maintained workflow assets with ownership, prompt/rule updates, and noise management rather than set-and-forget automation.
local_practice_implications: Coding-practice guidance should state that agent-authored code increases review-step responsibility.
Verification pages can separate AI review signal quality from human final approval.
Prompt/rules pages can treat review rules as living maintained assets.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Good candidate for a local practice note on AI-review maintenance burden and reviewer attention.

source.title: Staying Ahead of Adversarial AI Through Agentic Source Code Review

qualifying_findings.summary: Google Threat Intelligence describes an agentic vulnerability discovery harness that chains specialized agents through threat modeling and review, using asset inventories, SBOMs, architecture docs, threat intelligence, and a distilled knowledge base as context before human expert review.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Code-security agents need explicit context architecture and evaluation stages: reconnaissance, domain-specific subagents, threat-model synthesis, prioritized findings, and expert review.
local_practice_implications: Retrieval/tool pages can treat architecture docs, inventories, SBOMs, and threat intel as first-class context inputs.
Verification pages can model code-security review as a phased, human-reviewed pipeline.
Application-pattern pages can capture specialized subagent orchestration for vulnerability review.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Keep product and threat-intelligence platform details upstream; local page should focus on phased source-review harness architecture.

source.title: Harness engineering: how to make AI coding agents reliable and secure
source.date_basis: Visible publish and update dates on article page.

qualifying_findings.summary: Endor Labs defines coding-agent harnesses around context, tools, constraints, sensors, memory, execution environments, skills, subagents, sandboxes, and feedback loops, then argues that security is a missing sensor when agents install packages and run commands autonomously.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Local harness architecture should treat security checks as runtime feedback signals alongside lint, compilation, tests, and quality gates.
local_practice_implications: Application-pattern pages can expand harness components with security sensors and package-risk checks.
Context-architecture pages can classify rules files, system prompts, structured context, and tool exposure as harness inputs.
Verification pages can define success-silent, failure-verbose sensors that agents can use to self-correct.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, avoid broad harness ranking; use the security-sensor implication and instruction-file context taxonomy locally.

source.title: Agentic AI in enterprise risk management: a practical framework

qualifying_findings.summary: Dataiku proposes a visibility, defense, and governance framework that starts with inventorying deployed agents, ranking the highest-risk agents, implementing runtime controls and audit logging for one agent, and scaling from measured results.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Governance rollout should begin with an agent inventory and risk-tiered pilot rather than trying to govern every agent equally on day one.
local_practice_implications: Governance pages can define a 30-day pilot pattern around inventory, risk tiering, runtime controls, monitoring, and audit logging.
Adoption pages can connect agent rollout order to blast radius and measured KPIs.
Application-pattern pages can treat audit trails and oversight as reusable runtime components.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Treat vendor products as upstream-owned; local artifact should preserve the rollout pattern and governance fields.

source.title: Three Ways Camunda Speaks MCP (And Why the Direction Matters)

qualifying_findings.summary: Camunda describes three MCP integration directions: a process calls MCP tools, an MCP server exposes operational data, and a process becomes a callable MCP capability. It emphasizes visible tool selection, audit trails including discovery calls, human checkpoints for spend/commit actions, and fire-and-track receipts for long-running process invocations.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: MCP governance practice should model directionality, tool discovery, receipts, and checkpoint placement, not just whether an MCP endpoint exists.
local_practice_implications: Retrieval/tool pages can distinguish MCP-as-client, MCP-as-query-surface, and MCP-as-capability-export patterns.
Governance pages can require audit visibility for tools/list discovery and chosen tool calls.
Agent-workflow pages can use fire-and-track receipts for long-running tool-started work.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Potential local leaf on MCP directionality as a governed practice; do not duplicate broad MCP protocol coverage.

source.title: AI Coding Agents: Adoption Trends
source.date_basis: Visible article date in search result and page context; page body cites May-July 2026 survey period.

qualifying_findings.summary: JetBrains reports from its Developer Ecosystem Survey 2026 that coding agents have become common in professional developer workflows, with daily and weekly usage figures, multi-agent IDE integration, and a control/execution plane direction for agent-driven development across tools and environments.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Adoption guidance should assume heterogeneous agent portfolios and plan for toolchain governance, not a single assistant rollout.
local_practice_implications: Adoption pages can track multi-agent governance, not only per-product usage.
Application-pattern pages can treat IDEs as agent orchestration surfaces with multiple backends.
Governance pages can require policy consistency across local agents, cloud agents, IDE surfaces, and execution planes.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Confirm visible date during ingest because the opened page lines emphasize survey period more than publication metadata; exclude if date cannot be independently verified then.
